 ET Online Bhai Dooj 2026 today: Check city-wise tilak muhurat, puja timings, Dwitiya Tithi, Nakshatra, Yoga and Panchang details for November 11.
 Bhai Dooj 2026 is being celebrated today, Wednesday, November 11, marking the final day of the five-day Diwali festivities. Sisters across India are observing the festival by applying tilak on their brothers' foreheads and praying for their long life, good health and prosperity. Also known as Bhaiya Dooj, Bhau Beej and Yama Dwitiya, the festival is traditionally celebrated during the auspicious Aparahna Kaal. However, the tilak muhurat varies across cities depending on local Panchang calculations. If you are planning the rituals today, check the complete city-wise Bhai Dooj 2026 tilak muhurat, puja timings, Dwitiya Tithi, Nakshatra and other important Panchang details for November 11.

 Bhai Dooj 2026: Date and Puja Muhurat
 Festival: Bhai Dooj 2026
 Date: Wednesday, November 11, 2026
 Tithi: Kartik Shukla Dwitiya
 Auspicious period: Aparahna Kaal
 Significance: Prayers for brothers' longevity, happiness and prosperity
 According to the Hindu Panchang, Dwitiya Tithi begins at 2:00 PM on November 10 and ends at approximately 3:53 PM on November 11, 2026. The tilak ceremony is traditionally performed during the Aparahna period on Dwitiya Tithi.

 Bhai Dooj 2026 Panchang: Tithi, Nakshatra, Yoga and Rahu Kaal
 According to the Hindu Panchang, Bhai Dooj will fall on Kartik Shukla Dwitiya. The day is also observed as Yama Dwitiya. Here are the important Panchang details for November 11, 2026, as per New Delhi timings. 
 Panchang Details Timings / Information 
 Day Wednesday (Budhwar) 
 Festival Bhai Dooj / Yama Dwitiya 
 Month Kartik 
 Paksha Shukla Paksha 
 Tithi Dwitiya until 3:53 PM 
 Nakshatra Anuradha until 11:38 AM, then Jyeshtha 
 Yoga Atiganda until 3:40 AM on November 12, then Sukarma 
 Why Is Aparahna Kaal Important for Bhai Dooj?
Aparahna Kaal refers to the afternoon period of the Hindu calendar day. According to traditional Hindu beliefs, the Bhai Dooj tilak ceremony should be performed during this auspicious period when Kartik Shukla Dwitiya is prevailing.
 The festival is associated with the legend of Lord Yama and his sister Yamuna. According to Hindu mythology, Yamuna welcomed her brother Yama to her home, applied a ceremonial tilak on his forehead and offered him a meal. Pleased with her affection and hospitality, Yama blessed her and declared that brothers who receive tilak from their sisters on this day would be blessed with long life and prosperity.
This tradition continues through generations, with sisters praying for their brothers' well-being and brothers expressing their love through gifts and blessings.

 Bhai Dooj 2026: Puja Vidhi and Tilak Rituals
On Bhai Dooj, sisters traditionally prepare a puja thali containing roli, rice grains (akshat), diya, sweets, flowers and other puja essentials. The ceremony is generally performed as follows:
 Prepare the puja thali: Arrange roli, rice grains, a diya, flowers and sweets.
 Apply tilak: During the auspicious muhurat, apply roli and rice grains on your brother's forehead.
 Perform aarti: Light the diya and perform the traditional aarti for your brother.
 Offer sweets: Give your brother sweets as part of the celebration.
 Pray for his well-being: Sisters pray for their brothers' happiness, good health and long life.
 Exchange gifts: Brothers give gifts to their sisters as a gesture of love and appreciation.
 The rituals may vary across regions and families, but the central sentiment remains the same: celebrating the lifelong bond between siblings.
